question: Sal, acacia, and bamboo, which are types of Dry Tropical Forest, receive what amount of annual rainfall?
solution:
The correct answer is __**from**____** 51 cm to 151 cm**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dry Tropical Forests** are characterized by a** long dry season **and a** short rainy season**.
 
• **Sal, acacia, and bamboo** are some of the common tree species found in Dry Tropical Forests.
 
• These forests receive an **annual rainfall** ranging from** 51 cm to 151 cm**, which is **lower** than the rainfall received by other forest types.
 
• This are found between **10o and 25o** latitude.
 
• These forests are important habitats for a variety of wildlife species and provide various **ecosystem services**, such as carbon sequestration, soil conservation, and water regulation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sal** is a tree species found in tropical and subtropical regions of **Asia and Africa**.

 
 
• It is also known as **Shorea robusta**.
 
 
 
• **Acacia** is a genus of trees and shrubs found in arid and semi-arid regions of **Africa, Australia, and the Americas**.
 
 
• ​Based on the African species **Acacia nilotica,** it was first described by the Swedish scientist Carl Linnaeus in 1773. 
 
 
 
• **Bamboo** is a type of grass that grows in tropical and subtropical regions of** Asia, Africa, and the Americas**.
 
 
• **The Indian Forest Act, 1927** considered it a **tree**. Accordingly, cutting bamboo from outside forests and transporting it was made unlawful.
 
• **In 2017 **an amendment was made to the Indian Forest Act, 1927 and bamboo has been **removed from the tree category.**
